name: Linear
look: Ultra-minimal near-black canvas, four-step surface ladder, a single lavender accent used sparingly.

hero.title: The issue tracker your team stops working around
hero.sub: Vector is a purpose-built planning tool for product teams. Keyboard-first, offline-capable, and fast enough that nobody opens a spreadsheet instead.

features.title: Opinionated where it matters
features.sub: Every surface is designed around a single question: does this help the team ship this week?

items.title: Instant everything
items.body: A local-first sync engine keeps the entire workspace in memory. Navigation never waits on a request.

items.title: Keyboard native
items.body: Every action is reachable in two keystrokes. The command menu is the primary interface, not a shortcut.

items.title: Git that closes itself
items.body: Branch names, PR titles and deploy events move issues through the workflow without anyone updating a status.

items.title: Cycles, not sprints
items.body: Fixed-length cycles roll unfinished work forward automatically and surface the scope you quietly added.

items.title: Projects with a spine
items.body: Milestones, owners and a health signal that comes from real activity rather than a weekly status field.

items.title: An API worth building on
items.body: A typed GraphQL API, real webhooks, and an OAuth flow that takes about ten minutes end to end.

showcases.title: Planning that survives contact with the week
showcases.body: Cycles are fixed and automatic. Work that does not finish rolls forward, scope added mid-cycle is flagged, and the burndown reflects what actually happened rather than what was promised.
points: Automatic rollover with a scope-change log
Cycle review generated the moment it closes

showcases.title: The status field updates itself
showcases.body: Connect the repository once. Opening a branch moves the issue to In Progress, opening a pull request moves it to In Review, and merging closes it against the right cycle.
points: Slack threads that stay in sync both ways
Figma and Sentry links resolved inline

metric_lead: Measured across workspaces with more than fifty active members

gallery.title: Changelog
gallery.sub: Shipped continuously. A selection from the last two release cycles.

testimonial.quote: We moved forty engineers across in an afternoon and deleted three spreadsheets, a status bot and a recurring Thursday meeting. Nobody has asked to go back.
testimonial.name: Priya Raman

pricing.title: Pricing that stays out of the way
pricing.sub: Free while you are small. Priced per active member, never per seat you forgot to remove.

items.a: Import from Jira, Asana, GitHub Issues or a CSV. Identifiers, comments, attachments and status history are preserved, and a dry run shows exactly what will be created before anything is written.
Yes. The workspace is held locally and reconciled when the connection returns, so reading and writing continue on a plane or a bad hotel network.
Self-hosting is available on Enterprise. Most teams choose the managed service with data residency in their region instead.

items.q: What happens when a member leaves?
items.a: Billing is based on members active in the period, so removing someone stops the charge on the next invoice with no seat reconciliation.

cta.title: Start your first cycle this week
cta.sub: Free for up to ten members. No card, no sales call, no implementation project.

footer.tagline: A planning tool for teams that would rather be building than reporting.

notes: The canvas is the whitespace. Separate sections by lifting content onto surface-1 panels rather than by adding gaps.
Use the lavender accent on the brand mark, focus rings and one CTA per view. A second accent colour breaks the system.
Depth comes from the surface ladder plus a hairline border — resist drop shadows on the dark canvas.
Display tracking runs aggressively negative (about -4% of the size); the eyebrow deliberately runs positive to read as taxonomy.
Substitute Inter or Geist for the proprietary Linear cut, and JetBrains Mono for Linear Mono.
